body:
# the contributor audit of the first projective contact interfaces

Sources read in full:

- `candidate 22d923b6274e7758`;
- `candidate c56743c8d6824a18`, initial Sections1--5.

Both PASS as scoped. The second is the original support-ratio
perspective coupling, not the subsequent asymmetric or normal-dependent
center constructions. Its negative calibration must not be transferred
to those different paths.

## Product continuation capacity

Pointwise Jensen at (p,x), followed by integration over the SAME product
boundary, proves total cost at least |P| times source cost when p is the
arithmetic base centroid. The globally convex, z-independent continuation
attains equality, including a nonconstant source projective weight.
An exposed p instead admits exact localization by the positive part of
phi plus a sufficiently large exposing affine base function. Finiteness
and compactness bound phi simultaneously at all other fiber boundaries.

For general p, any balanced subcapacity w supplies the pointwise lower
bound T(P,p) phi(n,x), by Jensen and nonnegativity. For constant-in-x phi,
the hinge LP has dual constraints 0<=w<=1 and sum w(z-p)=0, and objective
sum w. Both sides have finite attainable optima; the polyhedral projection
argument justifies attainment even if a minimizing affine slope is not
bounded a priori. Multiplying its optimizing hinge by the positive
normal-dependent constant attains T(P,p)D. For nonconstant phi only the
lower bound is asserted except for the separately treated centroid and
exposed cases. This is a valid exact obstacle to a denominator-only
parity estimate, with actual complete product examples.

## Original perspective coupling

The support-ratio arguments in Psi_A and Psi_B have weighted average
1+a.m with weights h_A and h_B. Convex Jensen gives their average loss
at least h_M f(1+a.m). Every normal inequality for M_e follows; the
gauge inequality g_K<=g_M then gives the exact inclusion M_e subset K_e.
The source-in-interior-M hypothesis is genuinely used to make all
centered supports positive. It is not inferred from deepestness.

The continuum-normal first variation is correctly justified. Uniform
support-distance bounds sandwich the new body between the old body and
a (1-Ce) homothet. At a radial endpoint, testing every old active normal
gives the lower bound on fractional radial loss. A maximizing new normal
converges along subsequences to the old normal cone and gives the matching
upper bound. Thus the limiting rate is the MAXIMUM over that cone, not
an arbitrary selected normal. Unique-normal boundary points are a full
surface measure set, and the radial area formula and dominated convergence
give the integrated boundary speed. This proof needs no curvature.

Proper cap planes have surface-null intersection with the original
boundary, so their first loss is the strict cap trace. Supporting full
caps lose the entire body loss; supporting outside caps capture zero
d-volume and lose zero even if their boundary carries surface measure.
Those explicit statuses prevent using an incorrect closed surface
indicator. Pure integer caps are handled as full or empty fibers. The
same ambient integer tilt is retained in every input restriction.

Adding nonnegative convex fields at an input preserves inclusion, and
the first variations add on its one actual boundary. This justifies
the stated accounting of overlapping source/input roles without double
counting volume or claiming disjoint layers.

When a=0 all values of f used are1. The original fields are then the
original centered supports h_A,h_B,h_K and give a single affine fiber
homothety. Its determinant is the same (1-e)^d on every fiber, and it
fixes the integer base, so the normalized depth is unchanged exactly.
For a genuinely minimizing proper cap through the fixed source, the
first normal/base parameter variation of its pullback vanishes; hence
its fixed-cap loss is dQ. This checks the direct coarea moment argument.
The printed triangle numbers give12/(5409/200)=800/1803 as claimed.

No general cap-efficiency sign follows from either result. Newly proposed
asymmetric continuations and the normal-center contact-band path have
different input fields even at a=0, so this neutral-motion obstruction
does not apply to them without a new calculation.

## Subsequent exact constructions, Sections6--8: PASS

The normal-dependent centers have average y and each has signed support
distance s=h_M-n.y. This distance is positive on the support-gap band
Delta<h_K-h_M<r/2 where the cutoff is nonzero. The resulting fields
are continuous and convex in their physical variable, even though the
centers need not belong to the input bodies. Where the cutoff is1,
Jensen supplies s f at every midpoint. Replacing s by H=h_K-n.y costs
only e Delta f, which the original support slack Delta pays for e f<=1.
Outside this band the fixed positive support gap pays the bounded target
erosion for sufficiently small e. Thus the target gauge erosion is
EXACTLY compatible. No claimed o(e) repair or source-in-midpoint premise
is needed.

The asymmetric construction is simpler: choosing b_* to minimize a.b
and using the globally decreasing f makes its A-field dominate2H f
at EVERY actual midpoint. Its analogous B-field has the same property.
Any common nonnegative allocation of total one between these fields
pays the target normal constraint. The coefficient may vanish: the
radial sandwich and dominated-convergence proof still applies to
nonnegative speeds, and the unchanged input is treated exactly.

The source field, forced input field, and total original mass are all
retained. The triangle radii for the new normal-center path decrease
at equal absolute rates, unlike the old equal relative rates. Direct
expansion gives cap loss12, total loss27, and positive surplus12/601.
The one-input path has total loss261/10 and surplus252/601. Its old
fixed caps and its optimized caps differ by4e^2, so only their first
derivatives are equated. The underlying all-normal theorem and endpoint
slack supply the stated global scope. These different paths legitimately
escape the old affine-neutral calibration.

## Continuous normal allocation, Sections1--4: PASS

Read `candidate 72bbac9873894c0b`.
Allowing the coefficient t to depend continuously on n does not affect
the per-normal compatibility proof or convexity in x. The exact cap
losses are affine in t after pushing the actual boundary fields and
full/empty/proper loss selectors to the normal sphere. In particular
the sphere measures have no incorrectly assigned supporting-face mass.

The moment range for measurable0<=t<=1 is compact convex by weak L2
compactness relative to a single finite dominating measure. Continuous
[0,1]-valued functions approximate any such t in L1 of that measure,
including every atom. Hence strict vector inequalities in the range
are genuinely realizable by continuous fields; boundary attainment is
not overstated. The signed-measure support function is the positive
variation mass. Separating from the open positive orthant gives a
nonnegative cap-row mixture and the stated dual, with the correct sign.
Continuity on the compact probability simplex converts positivity for
every mixture into a uniform strict margin. This is a valid minimax
statement within this fixed convex erosion family, and is explicitly
not a swap of circuit selection or nonsmooth moving-cap allocations.

Section5's active-contact cutoff and weighted-overlap infimum also PASS.
The cutoff remains identically1 on a closed neighborhood of every zero
support gap. Outside that neighborhood the fixed positive support gap
pays the bounded target term, so every fixed cutoff and continuous
allocation gives an actual compatible small-parameter path. The pointwise
optimal endpoint cost is the smaller of the two normal-measure densities.
Continuous approximation preserves its infimum. Dominated convergence
then gives the precise remaining cost on Z={h_K=h_M}; the cutoff, the
allocation approximation, and the small shape parameter are chosen in
that order, with no unjustified uniform interchange. The inequality
(Gamma-beta)D_K>beta omega(Z) supplies a strict cap-loss margin from the
source alone. All discarded endpoint cap contributions are nonnegative,
while their ENTIRE volume cost remains. Mutual singularity on Z is a
correct sufficient zero-cost special case, not a generic assumption.
